title: Chapter 537
paragraphs: Chapter 537
Episode 145. Omen (6)
It seemed as if the sun had pierced the sky and descended directly.
The pupils of those watching the flame jewel formed by Jin were dyed red.
For the allies, it was a flame of hope and victory, but for the enemies, it was a flame of fear and defeat.
The runes left by Lior Zipfel spread light through Jin's body.
Those who had experienced the Sword Emperor City terror had already seen the runes dispersing like snowflakes once.
Then, Jin had also unfolded this magic and destroyed Kinzelro's flagship Gruenil.
And now, the final form of the annihilating heaven-burning jewel was an entity so massive that it couldn't be compared to what those in Sword Emperor City had witnessed that day.
Though they still hadn't recovered from the shock of the counter-current, Lior Zipfel's legacy had far surpassed that.
It had transcended human limits. Now, even such a phrase couldn't explain Jin's magic.
Divine magic.
With the will of two gods together, people could feel them from Jin even without knowing their names. Solderet and Klam.
Some people unknowingly put their hands on their chests, some kneeled, and some closed their eyes.
In this way, nearly everyone on the battlefield unconsciously paid homage to Jin.
Even though the war was ongoing, the act was almost involuntary.
They call the highest of all beings gods.
And behind Jin, the two beings sitting on the highest throne in the world of those gods were revealing their majesty.
Even if it wasn't a perfect manifestation, even the creatures and nature that felt the majesty of the two gods were showing respect.
The insects in the ground trembled, the birds flying far away cried out, and the wind stopped moving for a moment.
The darkness of the night retreated to avoid the shadow of Solderet.
So, humans in the middle of war had no choice but to pay respect as well.
Especially Murakan, being a dragon from Solderet, was deeply moved by this faint manifestation of Solderet, more than anyone else.
'Solderet......!'
He had never shown it, but since he was pierced by a friend's sword and woke from a thousand-year-long sleep. No, since Solderet's voice started to fade.
Murakan missed his god. Losing a god, as an existence derived from a god, was a pain that couldn't even be compared to a human losing their parents.
[Hey, Murakan. Are you crying?]
[What the hell are you talking about? Look straight, do you see any tears here?]
[Seeing how sensitive you're reacting, it seems you were crying.]
[Huh! Do you think I'm you, the King of Sky doesn't shed tears like that.]
New strength was infused into Murakan's barrier.

It was a temporary enhancement brought about by the will of Solderet embedded in the mirror, but to Murakan, it felt even more fulfilling than the moments when he had gradually regained his old strength after awakening.
The darkness was deepening. All the lights under the influence of the dark sky were quickly losing their power.
The torches went out and the flares that were being fired everywhere disappeared into the darkness.
The protective shields that were shining all over the battlefield like bubbles lost their color, and even the power of time unfolded by Quikantel faded.
It wasn't actually all gone, but it appeared so.
In the darkened landscape, the only source of light was Jin's magic.
Drawn by that fireball, Jin's body was floating in mid-air.
In terms of mere volume, the remaining 17 ships had the upper hand, but they looked like mere insects in front of the sun.
Despite being mass-produced, it was Zipfel's fleet. Not just a ship, but a fleet.
Until not so long ago, there was only one airship in the world, Cojec.
Starting with the appearance of Gruenil, they are now pouring out even mass-produced ships, but the prestige of the airship itself hasn't disappeared.
In war, an airborne fleet still means slaughter and terror itself.
Such an airborne fleet was being blocked by a single person and could do nothing.
[How dare you, Runcandel, inherit the legacy of the family's top mage...]
[You are disrespecting us!]
The opportunity to bombard, which was obtained by giving up half of the fleet, left only futile results and disappeared.
All that was left for the Wraiths was the last prepared chain magic.
[You are the ones who are disrespectful, not recognizing the will of the gods of infinity and magic in front of you......]
Can you still call yourself a mage?
Jin, continuing his words with a cold voice.
[You are just a piece of meat with strong magic, and nothing more than a deceased who defied the providence without fear. If your leaders were here, they would have shown respect as a human first.]
Jin's finger pointed at the red fleet.
Then the runes surrounding him moved towards the fleet. Looking up from the ground, it looked like the Milky Way was flowing.
Lior's runes left a mark on the red fleet and the wraiths.
At the same time, magic sparked from the wraiths' staffs.
No matter how great the magic power the Wraiths possessed, it was not dignified.
Therefore, their last chain magic and Wraith-only suicide weapon 'Explosion Star' couldn't reveal its original sharp radiance and went out.
It was just powerful, but it couldn't infringe on the majesty of the gods because it didn't have any elements to do so.
The Explosion Star couldn't even produce a small light like a candle.
Aaaargh...! Emitting monstrous screams, the summoned wraiths were oxidizing. Unable to destroy anything of the Black Emperor Star.
Only their suicide devices were exploding along with the 17 airships.
Hideous machines designed to kill humans exploded, spewing black fragments.
[Murakan, we must stop this!]
[Ah, why are there so many fragments! It's too wide, I can't block everything with a barrier...]
Murakan stopped talking and widened his eyes.
On each of the falling fragments towards our camp, on each of the countless pieces of death.
Lior Zipfel's rune characters were inscribed. Following Jin's will to prevent any of our allies from dying or getting hurt.
[...You and I have worried in vain, with Solderet's will being so vivid.]
Whoosh, Fssssss...!
Despite Murakan and Quikantel's determination to enhance their respective powers and shields, the rune characters perfectly decomposed the falling fragments in the air.
And then the fireball in the sky began to move forward.
Thousands of flames poured out from the fireball and wrapped around the destroyed ships.
The falling ships stopped their descent, but the ships that the flame tendrils did not grab continued to fall to the ground.
All of those were ships crashing towards the Imperial Army and the Zipfel Army.
"Ru, run...!"
"Evade, dodge!"
It was like a mountain was pouring down.
There was no thought of blocking it. A normal shield wouldn't stand a chance, only superhumans at the peak could handle the weight.
So the enemies were all shouting to run, to dodge, but that was just words blurted out in desperation, with no other choice.
Where are they supposed to run to?
Everywhere is blocked by the darkness of the dark sky.
In the darkness where you could barely see the person next to you, the enemies had no choice but to wait for death.
A more terrifying problem was that all they could not stop were the fragments of the red fleet.
From the moment the reverse sky was unfolded, not only the wraiths but also the ground forces had collapsed. Command had lost its value and orders were not delivered.
The Imperial Army did have some personalities. They followed the Emperor's orders, but the commanders wanted to end this war with minimal damage from the beginning.
Who likes war unless they are a madman? Especially a war that self-destructs the pillars of the empire.

Even if Zipfel didn't know, the Imperial Army was now certain of defeat. Therefore, the commanders of the Imperial Army wanted to save as many of their subordinates as possible, even if it meant their death.
It was closer to a belief that as a commander, it should be so, not a desire to repent in this unfair war.
But if that sun falls on the ground....
'It's annihilation, no one can survive...'
Not just the knights and magicians, but maybe even the emperor at the rear. If the flame tendrils spread to the rear, everyone left there as well.
Tens of thousands will die.
That unreal number of deaths was a scheduled reality.
The fact that such a large number of humans could disappear from the earth in just a few minutes was an issue that no one in the Imperial Army had ever thought about.
"How... can we avoid... such a thing."
"Jin Runcandel! We've lost, please stop, please!"
In the end, surrender declarations exploded from various parts of the Imperial Army. The commanders were crying out for surrender without the emperor's order.
Despite the world vibrating with all sorts of loud noises, Jin heard all those desperate and small voices.
And he immediately gave a reply.
[Regardless of the background and circumstances, the fact that you guys trampled on my friend and tried to kill him never changes.]
As if they were criminals standing on the gallows, the Imperial Army was kneeling and banging their heads on the ground, shouting in agony.
Please save us, please.
"Please...."
[So I feel like I won't be satisfied even if I burn you all, but it seems that my god has a different heart than me.]
As Jin slowly clenched his fist, the sun in the dark sky began to slowly fade.
At that point, the Imperial Army who had been prostrating screamed internally that they could live. Not a few were howling like animals and shouting thank you.
But Jin and the gods' mercy was not just merciful.
[I will take back the magic.]
The sun in the dark sky, which was dyeing the whole sky, was disappearing like a lie in an instant.
By then, there was not a single fragment left falling on our side, and the camp was in perfect order.
On the other hand, despite the disappearance of the sun in the dark sky, the fragments of the fleet continued to pour over the enemies' heads, causing continuous explosions everywhere.
Jin and the will of the two gods could have stopped all of those, but they did not.
That was the price the Imperial Army had to pay.
[So those who can survive, survive and run away. My promise not to kill those who retreat is still valid.]
Jin finished his words.
And the remaining Imperial Army were like bugs under a lifted rock, scrambling to run somewhere.
